learningObjective: Understand why a custom operator must provide a meta / FakeTensor implementation to be compatible with torch.compile.

canonicalClaims.claim: A custom op used inside a torch.compile'd function needs a meta / FakeTensor implementation to let the tracer propagate shape/dtype/device without executing real data; without it, the tracer either graph-breaks or errors.
conditions: The custom op is invoked via torch.ops.<lib>.<op>.
nonImplications: Does not imply the meta impl generates Triton for the op.
Does not imply Inductor can fuse the custom op with surrounding pointwise ops; opaque custom ops usually form fusion boundaries.

misconceptions.claim: Meta impl generates a Triton version of the CUDA kernel.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Meta impls only model shape/dtype; codegen is unrelated.

misconceptions.claim: Meta impls are only relevant to TorchScript.
Providing a meta impl makes torch.compile skip the real CUDA kernel.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The CUDA kernel runs at execution time; the meta impl is trace-time only.
They remain the standard mechanism in current releases.

implementationFacts: torch.library provides `impl(lib, name, dispatch_key)` for CPU, CUDA, Meta, Autograd, etc.
Meta tensors live on device='meta' and carry no data
Meta impls should be pure functions of the input shapes/dtypes/device
performanceScenarios: Correctly authored meta impls let torch.compile trace through custom ops without graph breaks.
